THREE FURTHER FALSE CLAIMS ARE NOW WRITTEN INTO tests/test_ownership.py AND tests/test_contract.py BY THIS ROUND'S EDITS: (a) O11's docstring says the two quoted derive.py formulas 'escape the textual half only because the character before the operator happens to be `)`' and that 'reflowing either one' would trip O11 -- the second formula has the bare identifier `run_windows` before its `//`, not `)`, and reflowing BOTH at their operators leaves O11 PASS at 166 sites (measured); (b) the same docstring says O11 with derive.py removed from the skip 'is PASS and reports ZERO findings ... at 2e8a63e, e4c5e4b, 7e902ba, 694f156, a2ffc08, dd6a396, f11ae02 and 40d2446' -- at three of those eight it FAILS with one finding, with the skip AND without it (the true and load-bearing claim, that the finding sets are IDENTICAL, is in the same sentence); (c) K15's prose says the old 'second name for the same condition' claim was 'true of two of the six' and then, one sentence later, distinguishes the two residue gates as ONE second name and ONE strictly weaker condition. findings.symbol: tests/test_contract.py::_k15_live_reason -- the bool() unwrap is applied to `reachable=` ONLY, not to `reason.test` (NEW, INTRODUCED BY ITEM 2's FIX)
findings.detail:
A DETECTION THAT EXISTED BEFORE THIS ROUND IS GONE. The new code unwraps `bool(EXPR)` from `reach` and then compares `ast.unparse(reach)` against `ast.unparse(reason.test)` UNCHANGED. So the moment the SAME wrapper appears on the reason's side, the two strings stop matching and the Gate falls out of rule 4 entirely. Two shapes flip from FAIL to PASS: (i) `reachable=bool(n > 0)` with `reason=(IMPOSSIBILITY if bool(n > 0) else "")`, and (ii) `reachable=bool(n > 0)` with `reason=("" if not bool(n > 0) else IMPOSSIBILITY)`. I ran both against the PRE-CHANGE file (the shipped file with the three-line unwrap deleted, which is exactly the 2026-09-04 code) and against the file as it ships: pre-change FAIL/judged=1 on both, shipped PASS/judged=0 on both. This is not hypothetical syntax: `reason=(A if bool(X) else B)` is the same idiom src/fabric/api.py already writes on the reachable side four times, and the four fabric Gates are one edit away from it. It also directly contradicts the comment the change ships with -- 'the two expressions are compared textually afterwards exactly as before, so nothing else is decided here'. Something else IS decided: two previously-judged shapes are now abstained on. No live site in src/ hits it today (my own AST census of all 15 computed-reachability Gates shows every reason.test is a bare expression) and rule 4's dynamic half reports ZERO findings at all 38 trees either way, so nothing is red -- it is a silent narrowing, which is the exact thing this round was called to stop. THE REPAIR, WRITTEN AND VERIFIED BY ME ON A SCRATCH COPY: normalise BOTH sides, and do it without changing ast.unparse's bracketing for anything else. In tests/test_contract.py, FIND (inside `_k15_live_reason`, the two lines that end the unwrap block):
            reach = reach.args[0]
        r, t = ast.unparse(reach), ast.unparse(reason.test)
REPLACE:
            reach = reach.args[0]
        test = reason.test
        if (isinstance(test, ast.UnaryOp) and isinstance(test.op, ast.Not)
                and isinstance(test.operand, ast.Call)
                and getattr(test.operand.func, "id", "") == "bool"
                and len(test.operand.args) == 1 and not test.operand.keywords):
            test = ast.UnaryOp(op=ast.Not(), operand=test.operand.args[0])
        elif (isinstance(test, ast.Call) and getattr(test.func, "id", "") == "bool"
                and len(test.args) == 1 and not test.keywords):
            test = test.args[0]
        r, t = ast.unparse(reach), ast.unparse(test)
It should ship with the two self-test cases that are red without it (the two shapes above) -- otherwise it is a widening with no witness, which is what the file's own standard forbids.

findings.detail:
THE CAUSAL EXPLANATION NEWLY WRITTEN INTO THE DOCSTRING IS WRONG, AND IT IS THE SENTENCE THE WHOLE 'KEEP THE EXEMPTION' ARGUMENT RESTS ON. Both cited formulas are real and both citations open -- src/spine/derive.py::run_windows_from_epochs (def at :377) carries `units.Windows(_windows_in_epoch(sysm) * int(sysm.configs["RUN"].epochs))` at :386 and src/spine/derive.py::opt_steps_from_windows (def at :580) carries `run_steps = max(1, run_windows // d_effective_batch_windows)` at :592, both bare indented, neither in backticks. But (a) the character before the operator in the SECOND one is not `)`: the raw line is `        run_steps = max(1, run_windows // d_effective_batch_windows)`, so the token immediately before `//` is the bare identifier `run_windows`. The real mechanism, which O11's own textual half makes plain (`_TXT` captures `name OP` and reports only `if nm in mine`), is that NEITHER formula puts a DECLARED CLOCK-LEVER NAME before its operator -- the first has `)` there, the second has `run_windows`, and `run_windows` is in no package's lever set (I enumerated the union: 32 distinct names, 35 declarations across 10 packages, `run_windows` and `effective_batch_windows` in neither). And (b) 'reflowing either one' does NOT trip O11: I line-broke both formulas at their operators inside the docstrings, with derive.py removed from the skip, and O11 stayed PASS at 166 sites. What actually trips it is REWRITING the first formula's operands so a bare lever name sits against the operator (`units.Windows(epochs * windows_in_epoch)` -> FAIL, 167 sites, one finding on src/spine/derive.py:386) -- a rewrite, not a reflow, and impossible for the second formula by reflow at all. THE POSITION ITSELF SURVIVES: the class is real, and h_k15's own _CLOCK_DERIVE fixture (`manage_every * rate`) proves it, so I am NOT asking for the exemption to be removed -- only for the reason beside it to be true. EXACT REPAIR, in tests/test_ownership.py, FIND:
    specifications and neither in backticks. Those two escape the textual half only because the
    character before the operator happens to be `)`; reflowing either one so a clock lever's name
    sits against the operator would make O11 report derive.py's own explanation of O11, which is
    the noise class the backtick rule two hundred lines below was written for.
REPLACE:
    specifications and neither in backticks. Those two escape the textual half only because neither
    puts a DECLARED CLOCK-LEVER NAME immediately before its operator -- the first has `)` there, the
    second the bare parameter name `run_windows`, which no package declares -- and NOT because of
    any reflow: line-breaking either formula at its operator leaves O11 PASS at 166 sites, measured.
    What trips it is a SPECIFICATION that spells a lever name against the operator, which is the
    shape _CLOCK_DERIVE now carries: rewriting the first to `units.Windows(epochs * windows_in_epoch)`
    takes O11 to 167 sites and ONE finding on src/spine/derive.py itself, which is the noise class
    the backtick rule two hundred lines below was written for.
